intro_en: This segment of the Israel National Trail climbs and descends two of the most beautiful mountains of the Lower Galilee: Mount Tabor and Mount Deborah. The fine views from the summits make up for the effort of the climb and descent. In autumn the harbingers of rain come into bloom.
character_en: (For those walking from the north) In the middle of the route – a fairly steep climb on the eastern side of Mount Tabor and a steep descent on its western side. Most of the route on Tabor passes in the shade of trees. Further on, climbs of moderate difficulty to Mount Deborah and Mount Yona. At the start of the route and in the Beit Keshet Forest area – walking on wide paths and comfortable dirt roads on a gentle incline.
transport_en: At the entrance to Kfar Kisch; in the Har Yona neighborhood of Nof HaGalil.
pois_en: The climb to Mount Tabor and the lookouts at the summit; the Church of the Transfiguration on top of Tabor; the autumn bloom of sternbergia and other rain-heralding flowers on the Tabor summit; the landscapes of Beit Keshet Forest and its winter bloom; the view and the woodland trees on Mount Deborah. In March: Nazareth iris blooming on Mount Yona.
important_en: It is not advisable to descend from Tabor after rain when the trail is muddy – the descent can be far too slippery.

There is a regular taxi service (20 shekels per person) from the western side of Tabor up to the summit and back; it is worth using when the trail is muddy and slippery on the descent, or to avoid the steep climb to the summit (for those coming from the south).
Next to the church at the summit there is drinking water and toilets. The church is open continuously from 8:00 to 17:00, even if some websites say otherwise.
description_en:
The Israel National Trail arrives from the deep part of Nahal Tavor (segment 9) at the access road to Kfar Kisch. The trail runs for a kilometer alongside the road, crosses southward over the road to Ein Dor, and climbs gently through the upper, flat part of Nahal Tavor as far as Gazit Junction.
After crossing Road 65, we climb a little through the village of Shibli and follow the markings toward Mount Tabor. The trail soon enters the wooded area and climbs through it fairly steeply for about 2.5 km up to the Tabor summit path.
After loosening up the muscles, we continue along a short, lovely level stretch among the trees; in autumn it is worth looking here for sternbergia and autumn crocus. It is highly recommended to walk along the road to the large Franciscan church, to take in its beauty and the story of the Transfiguration of Jesus as depicted in the pictures and in the New Testament (for more, see the Wikipedia entry). Nearby there is drinking water and toilets.
We go back along the road a little to the west, to the gate through which vehicles enter, and turn north, beside the remains of an impressive wall. After half a km, at the trail junction, a fairly steep but not long descent begins, down to the taxi station between Shibli and Daburiyya. Trekking poles are highly recommended. This section is not recommended for those who find descents difficult or who suffer from knee problems.
Continuing north, a gentle descent through a built-up area leads to Beit Keshet Forest. In the forest the trail follows a good vehicle track, part of it paved and used by the vehicles of local residents – take care when walking on it.
Beit Keshet Forest is one of the last remnants of the great Tabor oak forest that once covered the Lower Galilee. Nature-conservation struggles prevented extensive construction in the beautiful natural parts of the forest. Between January and March the area is covered with cyclamen, anemones and colorful blooms. The walk is mostly exposed to the sun, but there are many shady spots.
The final part of the climb to Mount Deborah is a little steeper, but follows a comfortable track. A coffee break facing the view at the summit, followed by a beautiful, slightly steep descent of about 600 meters to the road junction and the trail-marking junction above Nahal Barak Ben Avinoam.
We can finish here, or continue to the end of the segment for 2.5 km north, to near the cemetery at the foot of Mount Yona. In March there is a good chance of seeing one of the most beautiful of flowers – the Nazareth iris – in the area east of the cemetery.
nearby_en: A tour among the market and the churches of Nazareth, with many culinary options near the market and also further afield in the city.

Nahal Barak Ben Avinoam – anyone looking for a bit more "action" to end the route can replace the section between Mount Deborah and Mount Yona with the Nahal Barak Ben Avinoam route: a red-marked trail descending over rock steps, with many trees and spring blooms in a beautiful dry streambed. The stream begins at the north-western corner of Mount Deborah and ends at the Iksal–Daburiyya road. About another 5 km of walking to Iksal, where there is public transport.
author_en: Omer Shapira, guiding coordinator at the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
